lines.say: Today: modules, libraries, and pip, the tool that installs them.
lines.tts: Today: modules, libraries, and pip, the tool that installs them.

lines.say: In the terminal, the student types: pip install numpy.
lines.tts: In the terminal, the student types: pip install numpy.

lines.say: pip finds NumPy on PyPI, the online library of Python packages.
lines.tts: pip finds NumPy on PyPI, the online library of Python packages.

lines.say: It downloads NumPy and installs it on the computer.
lines.tts: It downloads NumPy and installs it on the computer.

lines.say: Now any program on this computer can use it, with import numpy as np.
lines.tts: Now any program on this computer can use it, with import numpy as np.

lines.say: And pip uninstall numpy removes it again.
lines.tts: And pip uninstall numpy removes it again.

lines.say: A module is a file of ready-made code. Import math, and you can use its tools, like the square root and pi.
lines.tts: A module is a file of ready-made code. Import math, and you can use its tools, like the square root and pi.

lines.say: There are three ways to import: the whole module, one tool with from, or a short nickname with as.
lines.tts: There are three ways to import: the whole module, one tool with from, or a short nickname with as.

lines.say: Libraries that don't come with Python are installed with pip. Type it in the terminal, not inside Python: pip install, pip uninstall, and pip list.
lines.tts: Libraries that don't come with Python are installed with pip. Type it in the terminal, not inside Python: pip install, pip uninstall, and pip list.

lines.say: This program uses Python's math library to work out how many strips to give.
lines.tts: This program uses Python's math library to work out how many strips to give.

lines.say: The comment says what the program does.
lines.tts: The comment says what the program does.

lines.say: import math brings in Python's math module. It comes with Python, so there's nothing to install.
lines.tts: import math brings in Python's math module. It comes with Python, so there's nothing to install.

lines.say: The patient needs forty-five tablets.
lines.tts: The patient needs forty-five tablets.

lines.say: Each strip has ten tablets.
lines.tts: Each strip has ten tablets.

lines.say: Forty-five divided by ten is four point five. But you can't give half a strip.
lines.tts: Forty-five divided by ten is four point five. But you can't give half a strip.

lines.say: math dot ceil rounds up to the next whole number. So the pharmacist gives five strips.
lines.tts: math dot ceil rounds up to the next whole number. So the pharmacist gives five strips.

lines.say: This line imports only the square root tool, so it can be used without writing math and a dot.
lines.tts: This line imports only the square root tool, so it can be used without writing math and a dot.

lines.say: The square root of eighty-one is nine. Python shows it as nine point zero.
lines.tts: The square root of eighty-one is nine. Python shows it as nine point zero.

lines.say: This error means the library isn't installed, or its name is misspelt: n u m p i, instead of numpy.
lines.tts: This error means the library isn't installed, or its name is misspelt: n u m p i, instead of numpy.

lines.say: And after import math, you must write math dot sqrt. Plain sqrt only works with from math import sqrt.
lines.tts: And after import math, you must write math dot sqrt. Plain sqrt only works with from math import sqrt.

lines.say: Which command installs NumPy?
lines.tts: Which command installs NumPy?

lines.say: The answer is B: pip install numpy. pip install downloads and installs a library. import only uses one that is already installed.
lines.tts: The answer is B: pip install numpy. pip install downloads and installs a library. import only uses one that is already installed.

lines.say: Let's recap.
lines.tts: Let's recap.

lines.say: A library is ready-made, tested code; a module is one file of it. You bring it in with import.
lines.tts: A library is ready-made, tested code; a module is one file of it. You bring it in with import.

lines.say: The standard library comes with Python, such as math: math.ceil() rounds up, math.sqrt() finds a square root.
lines.tts: The standard library comes with Python, such as math: math.ceil() rounds up, math.sqrt() finds a square root.

lines.say: Import a whole module (import math), one tool (from math import sqrt), or use a short alias (import numpy as np).
lines.tts: Import a whole module (import math), one tool (from math import sqrt), or use a short alias (import numpy as np).

lines.say: Third-party libraries such as NumPy, Pandas and Matplotlib come from PyPI and are installed with pip.

c1.heading: Modules and libraries
c1.callout: Ready-made, tested code you can import into your program instead of writing it yourself.

c2.heading: Three ways to import
c2.code:
import math
print(math.ceil(4.5))
from math import sqrt
print(sqrt(81))
import statistics as st
print(st.mean([250, 500, 375]))
c2.callout: Put your import lines at the start of the program, so every line below can use them.

c3.heading: Installing and uninstalling with pip
c3.code:
pip install numpy
pip uninstall numpy
pip list
c3.callout: Typing pip install numpy inside a .py file or at the >>> prompt gives a SyntaxError. Type it in the terminal.

lwalk.code:
# How many strips should the pharmacist give?
import math
tablets_needed = 45
per_strip = 10
print("Exact:", tablets_needed / per_strip)
print("Strips:", math.ceil(tablets_needed / per_strip))
from math import sqrt
print("Square root of 81:", sqrt(81))
